1.note: Amos is using the phrase **The words of Amos** to introduce this book. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new account.
“Tekoa” is the name of a town south of Jerusalem.

The implication is that Amos received this message from Yahweh in a vision. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [which he saw in a vision that Yahweh gave him]

Amos is using the expression **to the face of** to mean “before” or “previous to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [two years before the earthquake]

2.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Amos. It may be helpful to clarify that this is how he introduces his message for your readers. Alternate translation: [This is what Amos said]

2.q: יְהוָה֙ מִ⁠צִיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֔ג וּ⁠מִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יִתֵּ֣ן קוֹל֑⁠וֹ
2.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could connect the phrases with a word other than **and** in order to show that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Yahweh roars from Zion, indeed, from Jerusalem he gives his voice]

Amos is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a lion that **roars**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh thunders loudly from Zion]

Amos is using **gives his voice** as a common expression of the culture to mean “thunders.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he thunders]

Amos is speaking of **the pastures** becoming dry and desolate as if they were living things that could **mourn**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the pastures of the shepherds become desolate]

Amos is using this possessive form to mean that **the pastures** are the places where **the shepherds** feed their flocks. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the pastures where the shepherds feed their flocks]

Here, **the head** represents the top of the mountain called **Carmel**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the summit of Carmel]

3.note: Yahweh is using the formula **For three transgressions of …, and for four** throughout this chapter as a traditional Hebrew poetic device meaning complete or overflowing guilt. It does not mean a literal count of four specific sins. The number three shows a full measure, and the fourth pushes past the limit to trigger God’s judgment. If this would not be clear to your readers, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Damascus has done]

Here, **Damascus** represents the people who live in that city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people who live in Damascus]

Here, **the Gilead** represents “the people who live in that region.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the inhabitants of Gilead]
The pronoun **it** refers to Yahweh’s decision to punish. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

Yahweh is speaking of the way the people of Damascus attacked the people of Gilead as if they had been **threshing** them or crushing the grain they harvested. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their savagely crushing the people of Gilead]

The agricultural tools described here as **threshing sledges of iron** were heavy wooden boards studded with sharp iron points or stones dragged over grain to crush it. If your readers would not be familiar with what a threshing sledge is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with threshing instruments made of iron]

4.note: Yahweh is speaking of fire completely destroying Ben Hadad’s citadels as if it would **devour** them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy the citadels of Ben Hadad]

5.note: Here, **the bar of Damascus** represents “the defenses of that city.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I will destroy the defenses of Damascus]

Here Yahweh is speaking of removing rulers from power as if he **will cut off** the king from his kingdom, like a person would cut a branch off of a tree. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will remove]

Here, **the seated one** represents “the king” or “the enthroned one.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the king]

Here, **the scepter** represents “royal authority.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the one holding royal authority]

6.note: Here, **Gaza** represents “the people who live in that city.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people who live in Gaza]
See how you translated these same phrases in 1:3. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Gaza has done]

Yahweh is using the expression **taking into exile a complete exile** as a common expression of the culture to mean “deporting an entire population.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their deporting an entire population]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in 1:3. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

Yahweh is speaking of Gaza selling people to Edom as if they were objects and they could **hand them over**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to sell them] or [to deliver them]
Yahweh is using the term **Edom** to represent the people of Edom. Alternate translation: [to the people who live in Edom]

7.note: Yahweh is speaking of fire completely destroying Gaza’s citadels as if it would **devour** them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy her citadels]

8.note: See how you translated this same phrase, “I will cut off the seated one,” in 1:5. Alternate translation: [and I will remove their king]
See how you translated these same phrase, “the one grasping the scepter” in 1:5. Alternate translation: [and the one who has royal authority]

Here, **my hand** represents “my power to punish.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I will turn my punishing power against Ekron]

Here, **Ekron** represents the people of the city of Ekron. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people who live in Ekron]

9.note: See how you translated these same phrases in 1:3. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Tyre has done]

Here, **Tyre** represents “the people who live in that city.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people who live in Tyre]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in 1:3. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Tyre and the people with whom they had made a treaty as if they were **brothers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the covenant they had made as close allies]
See how you translated the very similar phrase, “taking into exile a complete exile, to hand {them} over” in 1:6. Alternate translation: [their deporting an entire population]

10.note: See how you translated the phrase **and it will devour her citadels** in 1:7. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy her citadels]

11.note: See how you translated these same phrases in 1:3. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Edom has done]

**Edom** is being used to represent the people of Edom. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people who live in Edom]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in 1:3. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]
The pronoun **his** refers to Edom, and the pronouns that follow in this verse refer to Edom as well. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Edom’s pursuing]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel, who were descended from Esau who was the twin brother of Judah from whom the Edomites descended, as if they were Edom’s **brother**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his kinsmen, the Israelites,]
Here, **the sword** represents “warfare.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in warfare]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **compassions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he refused to act compassionately]

Yahweh is using **his nose tore perpetually** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he continued to be very angry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he kept raging with fury] or [he continued to be extremely angry]

12.note: See how you translated the similar phrase **and it will devour her citadels** in 1:7. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy the citadels of Bozrah]

13.note: See how you translated these same phrases in 1:3. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things the sons of Ammon have done]
Yahweh is speaking as if the Ammonites, who were the descendants of Ammon, were actually the **sons of Ammon**. Alternate translation: [the Ammonites]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in 1:3. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

14.note: See how you translated the phrase **and it will devour her citadels** in 1:7. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy her citadels]

14.q: בִּ⁠תְרוּעָה֙ בְּ⁠י֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֔ה בְּ⁠סַ֖עַר בְּ⁠י֥וֹם סוּפָֽה
14.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the enemy will come with a shout in the day of battle, it will come with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind]

Yahweh is speaking of the violence with which the enemy army will attack as if it were **a tempest in the day of the whirlwind**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with overwhelming violence on that day of destruction]

15.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [he and his officials will go into the exile together]
